en: Conditioned by a state that is neither out-flow-free nor wholesome, an out-flow-free wholesome state arises by way of root condition.
Conditioned by a state that is neither out-flow-free nor wholesome, an out-flowing wholesome state arises by way of root condition.
(Abbreviated. There are two under root; ... pe ... there are two under non-disappearance.

Conditioned by a state that is neither with-outflows (anāsava) nor unwholesome (akusala), a state that is with-outflows and unwholesome arises by way of root-condition (hetupaccaya). [Under] root [condition], one; ... pe ... [under] non-disappearance condition, one.
In dependence on a state that is neither with-outflows nor indeterminate (abyākata), a state that is with-outflows and indeterminate arises by way of root-condition.
In dependence on a state that is neither with-outflows nor indeterminate, a state that is with-outflows and indeterminate arises by way of root-condition.
(Condensed. Two in the case of root-cause; two in the case of predominance …pe… two in the case of non-disappearance.
